observations:
Torah #45 LM2 is one of the shortest Torahs in the corpus — four sentences totaling approximately 300 Hebrew words. Its bechina structure is correspondingly minimal. After exhaustive review of every sentence in the source text, no independent conceptual domain emerges that is not already captured by the two proposed packages.

The two packages proposed cover every bechina statement in the text:
- Package 1 (שַׁבָּת / נְקֻדָּה פְּנִימִית / צַדִּיק): covers all three explicit bechina equations (שַׁבָּת = נְקֻדָּה, צַדִּיק = שַׁבָּת = נְקֻדָּה).
- Package 2 (שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַחֹל / עִגּוּלִים): covers the one remaining explicit bechina equation (הַשִּׁשָּׁה יָמִים = הָעִגּוּלִים).

Candidates considered and rejected for new packages:

(a) The evil domain — klipot / wicked / obstacles: The klipot (קְלִפּוֹת), the wicked (רְשָׁעִים), Jewish sinners (פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), and apostates (מְשֻׁמָּדִים) are all mentioned in the Torah. However, the Rebbe does not assign any of them a bechina equation. The phrase 'בִּבְחִינַת סָבִיב רְשָׁעִים יִתְהַלָּכוּן' is a proof-text citation (Psalms 12), not a bechina equation between two concepts. The klipot's behavior is described as eitza (they lead the wicked around = they cause them not to approach) rather than as a shared nature among multiple concepts. No evil bechina package is warranted.

(b) The 'journey to the Tzaddik' domain — travelers / obstacles / hope: The Torah's framing discusses people who prepare to travel to the Tzaddik and face obstacles. These are narrative/contextual elements (who has hope, who does not), not thematic concepts connected by bechina language. The concept of תִּקְוָה (hope) appears descriptively, not as a bechina of something else.

(c) The Zohar geometry — inner point / surrounding circles as a Lurianic structure: One might consider whether the Zoharic geometric structure (עִגּוּלִים, נְקֻדָּה) constitutes an independent mystical-structural package. However, in this Torah the Rebbe uses this geometry purely as a metaphor to support the teaching about Shabbat and Tzaddik. The circles and point are not given independent theological elaboration beyond their role as context for Package 1. They are best kept as Package 2 rather than elevated to a separate domain.

Conclusion: The two packages derived from the bechina graph (one from the dataset edge, one from the source text equation) are complete and sufficient for this Torah. The brevity of the source text leaves no room for additional independent packages.
